::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** [November 1890]  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown. Printed in the <i>[Girls’ Friendly Society Associates’ Journal and Advertiser](organizations/other_72.qmd)</i> (November 1890) 188.
:::

A BLIND GIRL

Dear Madam,-
Would any Associate or [Member](organizations/other_23.qmd), accustomed to cheer the blind, kindly get into communication with a Member, aged fourteen, a cottage child who is not in health for a blind school. She can knit, and read a little by Moon’s method, and has a mother and sister who can read letters to her. Her address is [Annie Nargate](people/person_917.qmd) [sic], Fergern Hill, Otterbourne, Winchester; but it might perhaps be best to write to her Associate, [Miss Jacson](people/person_1962.qmd), Yew-tree Cottage, Otterbourne, Winchester.		

I remain,
 C. M. Yonge.
